- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” rule: cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–3% for the first 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce forecast slope by 50% for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often overcorrects; apply “sentiment dampening” — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day if sentiment >0.75 and price < previous 3-day average.
